big_idea: Clear communication, in both speaking and writing, is a learnable, formula-driven skill, and eliminating ambiguity between you and your reader or listener is what makes messages land, persuade, and stick.

tool.label: The PEP formula
tool.text: A structuring formula Goodman describes as a method to get your point across clearly, every time, used to organize a message so the point is unmistakable rather than buried.
tool.note: One program in Goodman's Nightingale-Conant audio catalog, built for listening in short, practical segments rather than as a traditional print book; the exact expansion of PEP couldn't be independently verified beyond the publisher's own description.

ideas.title: Communication is a skill, not a gift
ideas.text: Goodman frames clarity as trainable technique rather than natural talent.

ideas.title: The three Ts
ideas.text: Help you appeal to any audience by tailoring your message to who's actually listening.

ideas.title: A four-step sales method
ideas.text: Offered for persuading others, applicable to products, services, or ideas, not just formal sales.

ideas.title: Breaking through writer's block
ideas.text: Five specific strategies are given, treating it as a solvable, tactical problem.

ideas.title: Sizing up your audience
ideas.text: Quieting your thoughts and assessing who's listening before you speak or write is framed as essential prep, not optional.

ideas.title: Stage fright, addressed directly
ideas.text: Gets practical treatment alongside the writing-focused material, since the program covers both speech and text.

try_it: Before your next important email, write one sentence stating your single point, then build the email around only that.
Pick one piece of stalled writing and try writing the ending first, or writing it as if explaining to a friend out loud.
Before your next presentation or difficult conversation, spend two minutes explicitly sizing up the audience.
Apply the four-step sales approach to something non-sales, like pitching an idea to your team.
best_for: People who want quick, audio-format tactics for business writing and speaking
Salespeople and presenters wanting a persuasion structure
less_useful: Readers wanting a print book to flip through, since it's an audio program
Those seeking deep theory rather than quick applied formulas

related.why: A sharper, book-length treatment of the same one-point clarity discipline
The psychological roots of miscommunication this formula works around
